plate_findings.evidence: T2 sagittal sequences of the brain demonstrating a hypoplastic corpus callosum

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Sagittal T2 MRI of a neonatal patient with hypomelanosis of Ito, showing hypoplastic corpus callosum, a recognized central nervous system manifestation of the disease as described in the figure caption and supported by the article's case focus. B: Sagittal T1 MRI of the same neonatal hypomelanosis of Ito patient, confirming hypoplastic corpus callosum, a known associated CNS anomaly of the disease.

In text: “crossed” hemihypertrophy with microcephaly on the left side of her face.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (a, b, c, d, e, f). a: Clinical photograph of bilateral forearms showing streaked/Blaschko-linear hypopigmentation, a typical cutaneous manifestation of hypomelanosis of Ito. b: Close clinical photograph of the left forearm showing the same streaked hypopigmented pigmentary pattern associated with hypomelanosis of Ito. c: Facial clinical photograph showing streaked hypopigmentation on the cheek with facial asymmetry/hemifacial overgrowth described in the associated hypomelanosis of Ito case. d: Clinical photograph of the buttocks demonstrating hypopigmented cutaneous lesions consistent with Blaschko-linear pigmentary mosaicism of hypomelanosis of Ito. e: Clinical photograph of the left waist showing Blaschko-linear hypopigmented streaks typical of hypomelanosis of Ito. f: Clinical photograph of the posterior left thigh showing hypopigmented streaky lesions consistent with cutaneous hypomelanosis of Ito.

On her left cheek is a prominent area of streaked hypopigmentation. The streaks are also seen on her arms, legs, and back. In addition, she exhibits “crossed” hemihypertrophy with microcephaly on the left side of her face, including microphthalmia of her left eye and a notably larger left leg when compared to the right leg. in_text_mentions: ticed at the age of two and five, mental retardation, pes cavus, talipes equinovarus, clinodactyly, eczema, inverted cilia of the eye, strabismus and reduced hearing. He later developed a ventral hernia, which regressed, he got glomerulonephritis with proteinuria at the age of seven and, at the same time, it was discovered that there were missing testicles in both scrota. At the present time, he is 13 years old and has developed leg length discrepancy (Figure 4), back pain and a syrinx corresponding to the conus as well as scoliosis (Figure 5), for which he has recently had successful surgery.
